_note: T10's German glossary. In repo, never shipped. One German word per concept, everywhere. de-short is the ring and overlay form, de-long the Settings row form. avoid[] are stems the validator rejects in any German value (case-insensitive, word prefix, after stripping placeholders and U+00AD). budget is the tightest fit class the term is used in, with the margin measured headless at 2.0 (worst of the three themes) where one was measured. source: 'Tobii' means taken from Tobii Dynavox Computer Control's own German on this machine.

entries.source: Tobii (Verweilzeit; its "Lernfähige Verweildauer" is the variant we avoid)
entries.note: Explained once, in the Dwell tab's description: the gaze rests ("ruhen") on a target. Crisis copy never uses the noun; it uses the imperative ("Blick ruhig halten"). "Fixieren" is blocked as an infinitive; fixation uses the noun Fixierung.
Noun only. A description says what happens: "der Blick bleibt ruhig".

entries.en: action menu (the ring of actions that opens after an activation)
entries.source: EyeCtrl (Tobii's "Interaktionsmenü" is 5 letters longer and names a different menu)
entries.note: "Ring" is reserved for the cursor ring: two gaze objects never share one German word. The action menu is "das Aktionsmenü" everywhere, its preview "die Vorschau des Aktionsmenüs".
Always says which one where it matters: "in Tobii neu kalibrieren" (the user's eye tracker) or EyeCtrl's own offset calibration on the Kalibrierung tab. Recalibrate = "neu kalibrieren".
The mapping a calibration computes. Not "Anpassung", which is adaptation.
The device is der Eyetracker; what it does is die Blickverfolgung. "Track Status" is Tobii's "Trackstatus".
The state is "pausiert" ("EyeCtrl pausiert").
"Caregiver attention needed" becomes "Bitte kurz nachsehen". The noun appears only in Settings prose.

entries.en: caregiver alert / eye-care banner / adaptation cue / toast
entries.de-short: Hinweis an die Betreuungsperson / Pausenhinweis / Anpassungszeichen / Meldung
entries.de-long: Hinweis an die Betreuungsperson / Pausenhinweis / Anpassungszeichen / Meldung
entries.note: Four different things on screen, four different words: never a bare "Hinweis" for more than one of them.
Gender-neutral by construction: say what is hard, never who. "struggle" = "die Bedienung fällt schwer".
Not "Tastenkürzel": that is a keyboard shortcut, one TYPE of Kurzbefehl.

entries.budget: A105: "2× Klick" +12.7. "Doppelklick" fails the ring at -1.2 (ink 0.85 DIP inside the arc against the 2 DIP rule), so the ring and its Settings-preview mirror say "2× Klick".
entries.note: The coordinator's call (b), 2026-10-11. The Settings row keeps Tobii's "Doppelklick". Shown on the ring-label sheet beside "Doppelklick (passt nicht)".

entries.note: On the ring the scroll icon carries "scroll", so the label is the direction alone.

entries.source: the user's pick B4 (T14, D8); Tobii says "Strg" too

entries.note: Descriptions say "der Blick", never "Ihr Blick", so a caretaker does not read it as their own gaze.

entries.en: cursor ring / circle (the ring that follows the gaze)
entries.note: Reserved for the cursor ring. English mixes "Circle" (rows) and "ring" (descriptions) for this one thing; German says Cursorring. The manual-selection ring is the Blickring, and a calibration point's progress ring is its Kreis, so no other gaze object is called Ring.
The ring shown at the gaze during manual selection. A different object from the cursor ring, so a different word.

entries.note: Bilingual on purpose, and the endonyms Deutsch / English / System stay identical in both languages.
